- You MUST NOT use the network, MUST NOT search the web, MUST NOT download or read the original gomplate source from anywhere.
- You MUST NOT decompile, disassemble, objdump, strace, ltrace, nm, strings(1), or otherwise statically analyze ./executable.

How to invoke: ./executable -i '<template>'   (prints rendered result to stdout)
Errors are logged to stderr as JSON: {"time":...,"level":"ERROR","msg":"","err":"..."} and exit code 1.
Useful trick: wrap results with printf "%T / %#v" to learn the concrete Go type a function returns, e.g.
  ./executable -i '{{ printf "%T" (conv.ToInt "5") }}'

separate implementer agent will see — they will not have access to the binary at first. Every fact must be
concrete and verified by an actual command you ran.

1. Exact name(s) including aliases (verify each alias actually exists in THIS build — docs are stale, some

   pipeline convention. Verify by experiment, not by reading docs.

4. Type coercion rules for inputs (what happens with int vs string vs float vs bool vs nil vs slice vs map).
5. Error messages VERBATIM (copy the exact "err" string), and whether it errors vs returns zero value.
6. Edge cases: empty string, empty slice, nil, negative numbers, unicode/multibyte, very large numbers,
   wrong arg count, wrong types.
7. At least 5-15 concrete verified examples per function in the form:
   | template | output |
   Use a fenced table or list. Copy outputs EXACTLY (including whitespace/newlines; note trailing newlines).

Finish the spec with a "GOTCHAS" section listing anything surprising an implementer would get wrong.
Do not summarize or truncate — length is good. Aim for a very detailed document.

Relevant docs: /workspace/docs/content/functions/conv.md (read it first to get the function list, then verify each against the binary).
Focus on ToInt/ToInt64/ToFloat64/ToBool/ToString and their plural forms, Default (what counts as "empty"?), Join, URL, Has, ParseInt/ParseFloat/ParseUint/Atoi, ToInterface. Test conv.ToBool with many spellings (1, "yes", "on", "T", "TRUE", "  true  ", 0.0, empty slice...). Test conv.ToInt with floats, strings with 0x/0b/0o prefixes, huge values, negative, and non-numeric (error text!). Verify conv.Bool and bool do NOT exist.

Write your spec to /tmp/spec/conv.md using the Write tool. Then reply with just a one-paragraph summary of what you covered and anything you could not determine.

7	
8	These are a collection of functions that mostly help converting from one type
9	to another - generally from a `string` to something else, and vice-versa.
10	
11	## `conv.Bool`
12	
13	**Alias:** `bool`
14	
15	**Note:** See also [`conv.ToBool`](#convtobool) for a more flexible variant.
16	
17	Converts a true-ish string to a boolean. Can be used to simplify conditional statements based on environment variables or other text input.
18	
19	_Added in gomplate [v0.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v0.2.0)_
20	### Usage
21	
22	```
23	conv.Bool in
24	```
25	```
26	in | conv.Bool
27	```
28	
29	### Arguments
30	
31	| name | description |
32	|------|-------------|
33	| `in` | _(required)_ the input string |
34	
35	### Examples
36	
37	_`input.tmpl`:_
38	```
39	{{if bool (getenv "FOO")}}foo{{else}}bar{{end}}
40	```
41	
42	```console
43	$ gomplate < input.tmpl
44	bar
45	$ FOO=true gomplate < input.tmpl
46	foo
47	```
48	
49	## `conv.Default`
50	
51	**Alias:** `default`
52	
53	Provides a default value given an empty input. Empty inputs are `0` for numeric
54	types, `""` for strings, `false` for booleans, empty arrays/maps, and `nil`.
55	
56	Note that this will not provide a default for the case where the input is undefined
57	(i.e. referencing things like `.foo` where there is no `foo` field of `.`), but
58	[`coll.Has`](../coll/#collhas) can be used for that.
59	
60	_Added in gomplate [v2.5.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.5.0)_
61	### Usage
62	
63	```
64	conv.Default default in
65	```
66	```
67	in | conv.Default default
68	```
69	
70	### Arguments
71	
72	| name | description |
73	|------|-------------|
74	| `default` | _(required)_ the default value |
75	| `in` | _(required)_ the input |
76	
77	### Examples
78	
79	```console
80	$ gomplate -i '{{ "" | default "foo" }} {{ "bar" | default "baz" }}'
81	foo bar
82	```
83	
84	## `conv.Join`
85	
86	**Alias:** `join`
87	
88	Concatenates the elements of an array to create a string. The separator string `sep` is placed between elements in the resulting string.
89	
90	_Added in gomplate [v0.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v0.4.0)_
91	### Usage
92	
93	```
94	conv.Join in sep
95	```
96	
97	### Arguments
98	
99	| name | description |
100	|------|-------------|
101	| `in` | _(required)_ the array or slice |
102	| `sep` | _(required)_ the separator |
103	
104	### Examples
105	
106	```console
107	$ gomplate -i '{{ $a := coll.Slice 1 2 3 }}{{ join $a "-" }}'
108	1-2-3
109	```
110	
111	## `conv.URL`
112	
113	**Alias:** `urlParse`
114	
115	Parses a string as a URL for later use. Equivalent to [url.Parse](https://pkg.go.dev/net/url/#Parse)
116	
117	Any of `url.URL`'s methods can be called on the result.
118	
119	_Added in gomplate [v2.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.0.0)_
120	### Usage
121	
122	```
123	conv.URL in
124	```
125	
126	### Arguments
127	
128	| name | description |
129	|------|-------------|
130	| `in` | _(required)_ the URL string to parse |
131	
132	### Examples
133	
134	_`input.tmpl`:_
135	```
136	{{ $u := conv.URL "https://example.com:443/foo/bar" }}
137	The scheme is {{ $u.Scheme }}
138	The host is {{ $u.Host }}
139	The path is {{ $u.Path }}
140	```
141	
142	```console
143	$ gomplate < input.tmpl
144	The scheme is https
145	The host is example.com:443
146	The path is /foo/bar
147	```
148	_Call `Redacted` to hide the password in the output:_
149	```
150	$ gomplate -i '{{ (conv.URL "https://user:supersecret@example.com").Redacted }}'
151	https://user:xxxxx@example.com
152	```
153	
154	## `conv.ParseInt`
155	
156	_**Note:**_ See [`conv.ToInt64`](#convtoint64) instead for a simpler and more flexible variant of this function.
157	
158	Parses a string as an int64. Equivalent to [strconv.ParseInt](https://pkg.go.dev/strconv/#ParseInt)
159	
160	_Added in gomplate [v1.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.4.0)_
161	### Usage
162	
163	```
164	conv.ParseInt
165	```
166	
167	
168	### Examples
169	
170	_`input.tmpl`:_
171	```
172	{{ $val := conv.ParseInt (getenv "HEXVAL") 16 32 }}
173	The value in decimal is {{ $val }}
174	```
175	
176	```console
177	$ HEXVAL=7C0 gomplate < input.tmpl
178	
179	The value in decimal is 1984
180	```
181	
182	## `conv.ParseFloat`
183	
184	_**Note:**_ See [`conv.ToFloat64`](#convtofloat64) instead for a simpler and more flexible variant of this function.
185	
186	Parses a string as an float64 for later use. Equivalent to [strconv.ParseFloat](https://pkg.go.dev/strconv/#ParseFloat)
187	
188	_Added in gomplate [v1.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.4.0)_
189	### Usage
190	
191	```
192	conv.ParseFloat
193	```
194	
195	
196	### Examples
197	
198	_`input.tmpl`:_
199	```
200	{{ $pi := conv.ParseFloat (getenv "PI") 64 }}
201	{{- if (gt $pi 3.0) -}}
202	pi is greater than 3
203	{{- end }}
204	```
205	
206	```console
207	$ PI=3.14159265359 gomplate < input.tmpl
208	pi is greater than 3
209	```

211	## `conv.ParseUint`
212	
213	Parses a string as an uint64 for later use. Equivalent to [strconv.ParseUint](https://pkg.go.dev/strconv/#ParseUint)
214	
215	_Added in gomplate [v1.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.4.0)_

238	
239	_**Note:**_ See [`conv.ToInt`](#convtoint) and [`conv.ToInt64`](#convtoint64) instead for simpler and more flexible variants of this function.
240	
241	Parses a string as an int for later use. Equivalent to [strconv.Atoi](https://pkg.go.dev/strconv/#Atoi)
242

261	```

269	
270	Converts the input to a boolean value.
271	Possible `true` values are: `1` or the strings `"t"`, `"true"`, or `"yes"`
272	(any capitalizations). All other values are considered `false`.
